title: Dash-light dimming: newer PMU-24 outputs O17-O24 cannot PWM
ask: Should the dash lights be dimmed by a small PWM stage on the dash controller board, now that the PMU's 7 A output O20 cannot dim them?
why: The dash lights are dimmed by switching their PMU output on and off fast (PWM) on output O20. ECUMaster's current PMU-24 pinout (v1.2, March 2024, and v1.3) says the 7 A outputs O17-O24 can no longer do PWM; the design was drawn from v1.0 (2023), which allowed it. Only the ten 25 A outputs can PWM, and all ten are taken: eight by heavy loads and two (O13, O14) held for the LS swap. On a current unit the dash lights would only be fully on or off. Nothing is cut or crimped yet. (This replaces block 01.53, which wrongly offered a swap onto O6: the 15 A outputs cannot PWM either.)
options:
(a) Dim them on the dash controller board: O20 stays a plain on/off feed and a small PWM stage on the display controller board dims the bus, the way the blower's speed is done. A few cents of parts and a board revision; keeps the pin plan and the LS channels.
(b) Give up dimming: the dash lights are on at full brightness with the park lamps. Costs nothing; loses the dimmer.
(c) Move the dash-light bus to O13 or O14, a 25 A output held for the LS swap, until the swap. Costs nothing now; takes back a swap channel later, so the swap would need another plan for it.
recommend: (a), unless the PMU in hand is a 2023 unit and ECUMaster confirms its 7 A outputs still PWM
stops: the dash-light dimming design and O20's configuration
